newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh was urged by the House Sports Committee to review the cabinet's sacking of the secretary governal of the Bangkok Asian Games Organising Committee. The committee is worried that the decision to remove Major-General Charuek Arirajkaran could backfire and lead to Thailand losing the right to host next year's Games (BANGKOK POST).

- Deputy prime minister Sukhavich Rangsitphol has become further embroiled in the Asian Games controversy, with the revelation yesterday that he had sought and gained Cabinet approval to exempt sponsorship contracts worth two billion baht from the scrutiny of the Attorney General's office, Cabinet source said. (THE NATION)

- Suspected arsonist Samrit Phetsathit was acquitted yesterday after languishing in jail for over 10 years while his case was heard. It is believed to be the longest trial ever in the history of the provincial court. Samrit is one of three defendants charged with torching the governor's residence in 1975. Two other defendents were also cleared of the arson charges. They were granted bail during the trial but Samrit was held because he did not have enough money to pay for a bail guarantee. (BANGKOK POST)

- Judges plan to block charter change plans. Chief justices from courts nationwide resolved yesterday to oppose all major constitution proposals related to the judiciary branch, but will wait until the complete draft comes out before spelling out campaign strategies, a top criminal court justice said. (THE NATION)

- The poor performance of the finance sector in the first quarter of 1997 will affect government revenue to the extent that further budget cuts will be required, the executive vice president of Bangkok Bank predicted. (THE NATION)

- Despite a falling current account deficit, economic figures released by the Bank of Thailand yesterday show a recovery is still far from sight. Economic pessimism slowed down foreign capital inflows last month, resulting in a slight deficit in the balance of payments, said Kleo-thong Hetrakul, director of the central bank's Economic Research Department. (BANGKOK POST)

- Eight labour councils yesterday demanded a 12.8 percent increase in the minimum wage for Bangkok and nearby provinces after the government decided to raise civil service salaries by five percent from October. (THE NATION)

- The Property Loan Management Organisation has scheduled the first batch of their zero-coupon bonds to be issued on May 2 with an expected value of 500 million baht to one billion baht, Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanonda said. (BUSINESS DAY)
